item.title: Accounting and Public Policy in a Contested World
item.content:encoded:
This special issue addresses the intersection of accounting and public policy in an increasingly contested global context. The call invites research that examines how accounting systems, policies, and practices respond to and shape public policy debates across various domains and institutional settings.

Appel publié par Journal of Accounting and Public Policy. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

item.title: AI, Policy and Public Value: Theorising the reciprocal relationship between AI and policy and its implications for public value
item.content:encoded:
Nisreen Ameen, University of Reading

Federico Iannacci, University of Sussex

Daniel Gozman, University of Sydney

James S. Denford, Royal Military College of Canada

This special issue examines how artificial intelligence embedded in public services shapes and is shaped by policy, and how these interactions affect public value. It addresses the bidirectional relationship between AI and policy: AI influences how policy problems are framed and implemented, while policy decisions configure how AI systems are developed and deployed.

The special issue invites Information Systems research that theorises AI as central to policy formation and enactment. It seeks to understand how organisations translate AI-policy ambitions into practice, how governance mechanisms enable accountability, and how these processes create, distribute or undermine public value—understood as plural, contested outcomes encompassing efficiency, equity, participation and welfare.

All submissions must include dedicated policy implications derived from evidence and analysis. Research should address how AI-mediated practices affect citizens and marginalised groups, and what trade-offs arise between competing values.

Appel publié par Information Systems Journal. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Creation and Distribution of Public Value
  • AI Use and the Production of Policy
  • AI Governance Beyond Regulatory Compliance
  • Policy Translation and Organisational Capability
  • Participation, Inequality and Contestation
  • IS Knowledge and Policy Formation

Timeline

  • June 15, 2027: Submission deadline

item.title: Advancing Wiser Consumption and Innovation: Consumer Wisdom, Wiser Innovation, and Public Policy for Flourishing
item.content:encoded:
This special issue invites research on the intersection of consumer behavior, innovation, and public policy. The collection seeks to advance understanding of how consumers can make wiser choices and how organizations can develop more responsible innovations that contribute to individual and societal flourishing.

item.title: The politics of regulatory simplification in the European Union: actors, processes and outcomes
item.content:encoded:
Steffen Hurka, Zeppelin University Friedrichshafen

Nir Kosti, LMU Munich

Brigitte Pircher, Södertörn University

This special issue examines why the European Union has struggled to reduce its regulatory complexity despite decades of simplification initiatives. Rather than treating simplification as a technical problem, the call frames it as a fundamentally political process involving conflicting interests, competing values, and strategic actors. The issue seeks to understand the gap between EU commitments to simplification and their limited concrete results.

The special issue invites research across three dimensions: the actors involved in promoting or resisting simplification and how they form coalitions; the institutional processes and mechanisms through which simplification efforts unfold; and the actual outcomes and conditions under which simplification succeeds, fails, or produces unintended consequences. Research employing qualitative, quantitative, mixed-methods, or computational approaches is welcome, and submissions from early-career researchers are particularly encouraged.

Appel publié par Journal of European Public Policy. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Who promotes or resists simplification, and why?
  • How do distributional conflicts and coalitions shape simplification efforts?
  • How is simplification politicised across institutional and societal arenas?
  • How do simplification efforts unfold within EU institutions?
  • Why do political commitments to simplification rarely translate into legislative change?
  • What role do Better Regulation instruments (e.g. impact assessments, Regulatory Scrutiny Board, REFIT, omnibus packages) play in shaping simplification?
  • Under what conditions does simplification lead to actual rule reduction?
  • Under what conditions does simplification result in symbolic reform, or even an expansion of rules?
  • How can the outcomes of simplification be measured systematically?

Timeline

  • July 22, 2026: Abstract submission deadline
  • June 1, 2027: Full manuscript submission deadline
